title: A tradition already sufficiently ready
meaning: Hope for a peaceful home comes closer when a familiar custom can be lived without every imaginable preparation being completed first.
text: Home may have a familiar form: preparing for weekends, meeting at the table and ending domestic tasks in your own way. The Hierophant in the physical position of Muladhara describes maintaining this routine. The World in energy tests your footing through demanding flawless completeness, with everything necessary and desirable ready simultaneously. The Star in emotions hopes for a warm, free life beginning after preparation. Yet hope moves away when the custom continually expands its conditions, leaving no simple moment in which both can already feel at home.

For example, anticipating a pleasant weekend, you prepare the room beforehand. Cleaning, arranging things, choosing music and making every treat all need finishing. **The peace you want can begin before perfect readiness.** An ordinary hour beside each other remains real despite an unfinished detail. Hope meets available life, and the household ritual stays a way of bringing warmth closer instead of continually promising it after one more compulsory preparation.

The difficulty is considering simple rest today an unworthy substitute for what you want. Preparation continues while less energy remains for the weekend itself. The ideal picture survives, but its meaning becomes harder to experience. Home offers more support when tradition is allowed sufficient completeness and actual life need not repeatedly move beyond the final unfinished detail. Its warmth can belong to the present too.
